text.p: These are the highilights in the Skopje press on Monday. Reuters has not verified those stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Macedonian economists ask consumers for patience and recommend traders not to incorporate expected inflation rate in retail prices, given the petrol prices have remained unchanged, with prices of oil and milk back where they were and prices of green market produce stabilised.
- Big staff changes in Macedonian public enterprises reflect recent government reshuffle, the paper comments.
- Water pollution in the Skopje region threatens to dry out waters and leave rivers with no living species.

- Archbishop of the Macedonian Orthodox Church Mihail, at all-Macedonian meeting in Trnovo, said he hoped that by force of the European laws "Macedonia will see justice done and Macedonians in all neighbouring countries will be recognized."

- Ethnic Albanian parties PDP and DPA condemned the postponement of the parliament session on the events in Gostivar claiming the ruling SDSM wants to buy time and disregard facts the police had intervened beyond its powers.
- Leaders of the ethnic Albanian parties from Macedonia congratulated the new Albanian leadership.
- Public pharmacies are empty with not a single medicine available on prescription.
- Macedonian deputy justice minister Mersim Polozani's wife Emina suspected of involvement in a visa forgery scandal.

- Macedonian commercial banks have not extended credits for more than four months awaiting adoption of mortgage laws to enforce collection of mortgage payment within 24 hours. Banks insist they have no guarantees for repayment of credits while the current legal vacuum exists. Macedonian firms owe to banks almost $150 million. -- Skopje newsroom, + 389 1 117 876
